title: PCI DSS v4.0.1 (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard) - paraphrased demo excerpt
rawText:
Paraphrased summary of selected PCI DSS v4.0.1 requirements, written for demonstration. It keeps the official requirement numbers but is not the text of the standard, which is copyright of the PCI Security Standards Council. Consult the official standard before relying on it.

Requirement 3.2.1 Keep stored account data to a minimum
Account data must be stored only where there is a documented business need. A retention period must be defined for each kind of stored account data, and data older than its retention period must be securely deleted or made unrecoverable by a process that runs at least every three months.

Requirement 3.3.1 Do not keep sensitive authentication data after authorisation
Sensitive authentication data must not be stored once a card authorisation has completed, even if it is encrypted. This includes the full contents of the magnetic stripe or chip, the card verification code (the three or four digit value printed on the card), and any PIN or PIN block.

Requirement 3.4.1 Mask the card number when it is displayed
Wherever the primary account number (PAN) is displayed or written out, it must be masked so that at most the first six and last four digits are visible, unless a person has a documented business need to see the full number.

Requirement 3.5.1 Make stored card numbers unreadable
The PAN must be rendered unreadable anywhere it is stored, including in databases, files, backups and logs. Acceptable methods are one-way hashes of the entire PAN using a keyed cryptographic hash, truncation, index tokens, or strong cryptography with managed keys.

Requirement 4.2.1 Protect card numbers sent over public networks
Strong cryptography must protect the PAN whenever it is transmitted over open, public networks. Only trusted keys and certificates may be accepted, and the protocol in use must support only secure versions and configurations. Plain HTTP is never used to send account data.

Requirement 8.2.1 Give every user a unique ID
Every user must be assigned a unique ID before being allowed to access system components or cardholder data, so that every action can be traced to one individual.

Requirement 8.2.2 Do not use shared or generic accounts
Group, shared or generic accounts and their credentials must be used only when strictly necessary on an exception basis; their use must be approved and limited in time, and the identity of the individual must be confirmed before access is granted.

Requirement 8.4.2 Require multi-factor authentication for access to cardholder data
Multi-factor authentication must be required for all access into the cardholder data environment.

Requirement 10.2.1 Keep audit logs of access to cardholder data
Audit logs must be enabled and must record every individual user's access to cardholder data, all actions taken by administrators, and every use of authentication and identification mechanisms.
